notes: Andy's plan names a ClimateMaster Tranquility 30 as the basis of design and assumes a downflow unit. This is the unit Greg quoted and Maxwell sent Andy on 8/14/2026.

Greg's quote MMUL8476-4 is for GZT048J11LM1CCS, which is a left hand return. This layout needs the right hand return version: standing at the water connection end, the return and filter are on the right. The unit is not ordered yet, so ask Greg to quote the right hand model and confirm which side the service panels are on.

Service access from the GZT manual (p.17): 2 ft clear in front of the controls and compressor panel, which is the south (connection) end; 2 ft beside the blower door, which with end discharge is on the west side at the north end; working room for the reversing valve and heat exchanger on the west side and for the TXV and filter drier on the east side, both near the south end. The west aisle is 2 ft, the return plenum stops at the coil so the TXV corner is open, and the ERV intake duct runs along the west wall just above the cabinet's height, so the aisle is clear up to about 2-1/2 ft over the deck. STILL SHORT: the ERV hangs 17 in in front of the controls end and has to move.

Condensate: the drain is at the north end, the EZ-Trap needs 6-1/2 in of height so the unit sits on a 6-1/2 in pad, and the unit tilts 1/4 to 1/2 in toward the drain (p.19, p.35). Over a finished ceiling a secondary drain pan under the unit is the usual code answer; the manual shows it as optional.

Turned 90 degrees (Maxwell, 11/18/2026): supply out the north end toward the trunk, water and desuperheater connections on the south end right above the flow center, return and filter on the east side, service panels facing a 2 ft aisle along the west wall.

notes: Greg's alternative: RenewAire EV Premium M, about $1,800.
Dimensions are approximate: the maker's spec sheet was not reachable, so the size comes from the product class.

The bathrooms exhaust through this unit instead of separate fans (Maxwell, 11/17/2026). The code allows it because the ERV sends that air outdoors; it has to run continuously at 20 CFM or more per bathroom (IRC table M1505.4.4).

Fresh air goes into the supply plenum, not the attic (Maxwell, 11/18/2026). Panasonic's instructions say the furnace blower should run whenever the ERV runs when it is tied into the ductwork, and Building Science Corp. calls for an interlock and a motorized damper on a supply side connection. The heat pump's ECM blower can idle at low speed for this. Andy should confirm the ERV can push against the supply plenum's pressure; the fallback is the return plenum, which the code also counts as supply ventilation (IRC M1505.4.1).

One fan pulls from all three bathrooms, so the whole exhaust duct is under suction and air cannot be pushed from one bathroom into another. Backdraft dampers are for separate fans that share a duct. Each branch gets a balancing damper to set its airflow.

Set out to Panasonic's installation instructions (Maxwell, 11/18/2026): the two outdoor hoods are more than 10 ft apart, every duct connection has 2 ft or more of straight run before its first elbow, the outdoor ducts are insulated, the unit hangs level on chains inside the conditioned attic, and the intake is well over 6 ft from the dryer and range hood outlets.

A backdraft damper in the fresh air duct stops the heat pump's blower from pushing supply air backward through the ERV. With the blower off, the ERV's own fan still sends the fresh air down the supply trunk to every register, so it works without the heat pump running. Three baths plus whole house ventilation (about 75 CFM for this size and bedroom count) is near the top of a 100 CFM unit, so Andy should confirm the size. The range hood cannot connect here, it has its own duct outdoors.
info.placement: In line with the heat pump, just south of it, hung at the height of its top. Andy drew it west of HP-01.

info.model: 10 in round flex
notes: Bedroom 3's grille moved from its south wall, next to the bed, to its north wall (Maxwell, 11/17/2026). It shares that wall with bedroom 2, so the stacks rise side by side into the trusses over bedroom 3 and join there: bedroom 2's 6 in flex crosses one truss into bedroom 3's bay and tees into a 10 in flex that runs south in that bay, parallel to the trusses, to the return plenum box at the heat pump.
Bedroom 3 has two grilles and two stacks (duct balance check, 11/18/2026): a 14 x 2-1/2 in stack is all a 2x4 wall holds, and one of them alone passed only about three quarters of the room's 127 CFM.

Round flex duct: a rectangular duct cannot pass through open web floor trusses, and 11-7/8 in trusses leave about 8-7/8 in between the chords. Runs that go north to south lie in one truss bay, parallel to the trusses, where a bigger round fits. Runs that cross the trusses go through the web openings at 6 in or less. For reference, SBCA's floor truss guidance lists about 5-5/8 in round through the end panel of a 12 in deep truss and 7 to 8 in through the larger interior panels, so the truss maker should confirm the opening sizes on the truss drawings, or build a duct chase where these runs cross. Flex is fine for returns inside the conditioned envelope if it is pulled tight with gentle bends. Sizes are ASSUMED until Andy or the HVAC installer sizes them.

info.model: 8 in round exhaust
notes: 8 in smooth galvanized duct straight up inside the hood's chimney cover, through the roof to the roof mounted blower. One straight run with no elbows is the quietest and moves the most air. A range hood may not connect to the ERV or the return: IRC M1503 (adopted in the Ohio residential code) requires its own duct to the outdoors. The blower's own gravity damper closes it when off; an insulated backdraft damper at the hood is worth adding in a house this tight. Hood not picked yet. It needs to be a liner or insert sold for a remote blower (no fan inside the hood), 400 CFM or less ASSUMED so no makeup air is required. The chimney cover is drawn 14-3/8 in square so the silencer fits inside it; a stock chimney is usually narrower, so it may need to be a custom or extended cover.
